transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) http5xx FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: Latency is up across many services, but the slowest ones are upstream planners, not the leaves. Next I'll check the call graph to see which edges carry the added time.

input.reflection: Abnormal vs normal avg/p95 latency: big increases in ts-route-plan (avg 1422ms vs 126, p95 8588 vs 492), ts-travel-plan (1224 vs 141), ts-travel-service (448 vs 24), ts-food-service (955 vs 18), ts-preserve (788 vs 98), ts-basic (99 vs 19), ts-station (32 vs 2), ts-train-food (36 vs 2), ts-seat (65 vs 13), ts-auth (37 vs 20), ts-travel2 (90 vs 26). Leaves like ts-route-service, ts-config, ts-order, ts-price look normal. No ERROR status codes in traces, only 2 http 5xx on travel-service. So this is a latency fault. Next: call graph parent->child to find which edge/service's own work is slow (self time). Need to join spans on parent_span_id.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name parent_svc, p.span_name parent_span, c.service_name child_svc, c.span_name child_span, count(*) n, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) parent_ms, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) child_ms FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY parent_ms DESC LIMIT 40

content.text: The slow path runs through ts-travel-service `GET /routes/{tripId}`. Its own repository call is about 3 ms, so the time sits in a child call. I'll check that child and the infrastructure metrics next.

input.query: SELECT c.service_name, c.span_name, c.attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) ms, round(avg(p.duration)/1e6,1) parent_ms FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-travel-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 30

content.text: The `GET` client span in ts-travel-service takes about 2.4 s, but the ts-route-service server span it calls takes only 23 ms, so the gap is outside both work spans. Next I'll check pod-level metrics for the involved services.

content.text:
## Investigation findings

The telemetry points to one primary root cause: a roughly 2.3 s added delay on ts-travel-service's outbound HTTP call to ts-route-service. This is a latency fault, not an error fault. I found no evidence of a second independent root cause, though there is a smaller secondary slowdown in ts-seat-service.

### Affected endpoints and services
- **User-facing paths (ui-dashboard, from loadgenerator):** travelPlan/quickest and /cheapest (avg ~6–7.4 s, p95 ~2.4 s+), travelPlan/minStation (~2.0 s), food lookup (~1.9 s), preserve (~2.3 s).
- **Service-level latency (abnormal vs normal avg):**
  - ts-route-plan: 1422 ms vs 126 ms
  - ts-travel-plan: 1224 ms vs 141 ms
  - ts-travel: 448 ms vs 24 ms
  - ts-food: 955 ms vs 18 ms
  - ts-preserve: 788 ms vs 98 ms
  - ts-travel2, ts-basic, ts-seat, ts-station, ts-train-food: all clearly elevated
- **Unaffected:** ts-route-service itself, ts-config, ts-order, ts-price, ts-user, ts-contacts, and others remain near baseline.
- **Errors:** no meaningful error signal. Only 2 HTTP 5xx in the whole abnormal trace set, both in ts-travel-service.

### Root cause: ts-travel-service → ts-route-service outbound call
- Its `GET` client span (travel → route, `/api/v1/routeservice/routes/{routeId}`) averages **2430 ms** and never drops below **2307 ms** in any minute of the window. Normal is about 6 ms.
- The ts-route-service server span for the same call takes only **~23 ms** (normal ~4 ms). The ~2.4 s gap lies on the travel-service side of the call, before route-service begins work.
- ts-travel-service's own work is fast: `TripRepository.findByTripId` ~3 ms, and `Transaction.commit` ~1.4 ms. Its self-time is almost entirely this outbound `GET`, about 2408 ms per span.
- Supporting metrics:
  - `http.client.request.duration` for travel-service averages 0.39 s (normal 0.026 s).
  - `db.client.connections.use_time` rises for travel-service (mean 836 vs 68) and route-service (max 2392 vs 499).
  - Pool usage is about 5 of 10, with no pending requests.
- Pod CPU and memory for travel and route are close to normal. Route-service `queueSize` is actually lower than normal. There are no restarts and no OOM signals, so route-service is not overloaded.

**Caveat:** the data localises the delay to the travel → route edge, on the travel-service client side. It does not fully separate a client-side configuration or pool problem in ts-travel-service from transport latency on that edge. Either way, the origin is that edge, not route-service's processing.

### Propagation
The slow edge is upstream of most of the slow user paths:
- travel-service → route-plan-service (route-plan's `GET` to travel-service waits ~2.3 s), which in turn slows travel-plan-service's `POST` to route-plan (quickest/cheapest routes, ~5.2–5.5 s).
- travel-plan-service → ui-dashboard (quickest/cheapest/minStation).
- travel-service → food-service (`GET /routes/{tripId}`, ~2.6 s), which slows ui-dashboard's food endpoint.
- travel-service → preserve-service (`trip_detail`, ~1.7 s), which slows the preserve endpoint.
- Route-plan's `getMinStopStations` and ui-dashboard's own self-time are fan-in effects of waiting on these calls, not origins.

### Secondary, lower-confidence contributor: ts-seat-service
- Seat's controller time rises from ~20 ms to ~104 ms, and its outbound `GET` to ts-config-service shows an ~82 ms gap (normal ~13 ms).
- ts-config-service's own server time is only ~8 ms (normal ~3.6 ms).
- This looks like a minor, separate slowdown. It is much smaller than the travel → route delay and may also be a downstream effect of the same resource pressure.
